findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with no referenceId deletes the DB row immediately and skips the cancel flag
findings.body: When referenceId is null the function deletes the workflowReminder row directly. For reminders that were never scheduled in SendGrid (scheduled=false, cron-pending), this is fine, but the function is also called with reminder.referenceId for already-scheduled reminders in the non-immediate path, which only sets cancelled=true and never cancels the SendGrid send. The cron then cancels within the hour, but the email can still go out for reminders scheduled more than an hour ahead only if the cron misses them; more importantly the sendAt delay is ignored, so the deletion relies entirely on the cron job running every 15 minutes.

findings.title: Immediate cancel path returns without deleting the reminder row
findings.body: In the immediateDelete branch the SendGrid cancel request is sent but the workflowReminder row is not removed and cancelled is not set. The row keeps referenceId pointing to a batch that is already cancelled, so later operations (cron, reschedule lookups) act on stale state and the row lingers until the scheduledDate cleanup.

findings.title: Cron cancels reminders one by one and aborts the whole batch on first error
findings.body: The loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside one try block. If any single SendGrid cancel fails (for example the batch was already sent or was already cancelled), the catch logs and the remaining cancelled reminders in the loop are never cancelled, and the workflowRemindersToDelete promises for earlier ones are not awaited. They will be retried on the next run only if the failing one is still flagged, so other reminders can keep getting sent.

findings.title: Cancelled reminders with no referenceId are never deleted or cancelled
findings.body: remindersToCancel is selected by cancelled=true and scheduledDate only. Rows with null referenceId are passed to client.request with batch_id null, which fails, and the catch then aborts the loop, so one bad row blocks all others.

findings.title: Promise array of prisma delete is built but Prisma client calls are lazy and typed oddly
findings.body: The array is typed as Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient, and the delete promises are only awaited after all SendGrid calls have completed, so a failure in the loop leaves them unawaited and rows may be left behind silently.

findings.title: SMS reminder row is deleted immediately while Twilio cancel may have failed
findings.body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the workflowReminder row unconditionally after twilio.cancelSMS. If cancelSMS throws, the catch swallows the error and the row is not deleted either, but more importantly the row is deleted even when the Twilio message is still pending in the non-cancelled path, so there is no record to retry. Also SMS cancellation is not deferred via the cancelled flag as emails are, so behavior is inconsistent.

findings.title: Workflow delete uses immediate email cancel while the scheduledReminders query only returns scheduled rows
findings.body: Deleting a workflow passes immediateDelete=true for email reminders, which hits the SendGrid cancel path that does not remove the DB row. The workflow is then deleted with deleteMany which cascades reminders, but the per-reminder cancel is fired without await and errors are only logged, so SendGrid sends may still go out.

findings.title: Removed event types no longer scope reminder deletion to the user
findings.body: The previous deleteMany was restricted by booking.userId = ctx.user.id. The replacement removes the DB-side deletion entirely for these reminders, so non-scheduled (scheduled=false) rows for disabled event types are never removed from the database by this path, leaving stale cron-pending rows that the scheduleEmailReminders job will still process and send.

findings.title: Edited-step reminder cancellation uses forEach with async callbacks
findings.body: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) does not await deleteScheduledEmailReminder or deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so the mutation returns before reminders are cancelled and any error becomes an unhandled rejection. The previous explicit deleteMany on workflowReminder was also removed here, so rows for edited steps are no longer removed in the SMS path reliably.

findings.title: Large block of indentation-only changes in testAction comment
findings.body: The diff reindents commented-out code in testAction, which is unrelated to the fix and inflates the review surface without functional change.

findings.title: Error message does not match the operation performed
findings.body: The catch logs 'Error canceling reminder' for every branch, including the DB delete path, making failures in the cron-marking step hard to distinguish from SendGrid failures.

findings.title: New cancelled column is nullable Boolean with no default
findings.body: cancelled is Boolean? with no default, so existing rows are NULL. The cron filter cancelled: true excludes NULLs correctly, but code that treats the flag as tri-state adds ambiguity; a non-null default false would be safer.

findings.title: Reschedule cancels previous reminders with immediateDelete=true inside try that cannot catch async errors
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder is async but is called without await inside forEach within a try block, so the try/catch never catches its rejections. The call is also made with immediateDelete true, cancelling in SendGrid without removing the DB row, leaving stale rows referencing a cancelled batch.
